source.title: The Sign Code: The Hidden Binary Nature of Deep Networks
source.authors: N. Göring; Shuo Zhang; Roi Holtzman; Yoonsoo Nam; Ard A. Louis

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices. No apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own experiments relating sign-code structure and interventions to classification and generalization. These are related to the catalog claim’s generalization subject, but do not test any of its eight specified versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports no random-label training, interpolation-threshold sweep, optimizer or batch-size comparison, dropout test, magnitude-aware sharpness comparison, or memorized-example removal. It does report sign-code classification, sign/magnitude interventions, and a sign-repulsion training intervention; these results are recorded under fits_no_version because none measures a behavior specified by V1–V8.
record.test_reason: The study tests sign-code sufficiency, activation interventions, and sign-code geometry. None measures V1–V8. Its width sweeps measure sign-only/full-model agreement rather than test error beyond interpolation; its perturbations alter activations rather than measuring magnitude-aware weight sharpness. References to random-label memorization and sharpness provide background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors further argue that class-coherent sign geometry is necessary for generalization in the studied models, while acknowledging that repulsion may affect correlated properties. Magnitude-replacement robustness is strongest in residual networks and depends on enforcing the cached clean sign trajectory.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates sign-code sufficiency, sign/magnitude interventions, and sign-code geometry rather than the original studies’ random-label, optimizer, architecture, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Sign-code sufficiency varies with depth and width; magnitude-replacement effects vary by architecture and activation; sign-repulsion outcomes vary by activation and proxy.

fits_no_version.finding: Last-layer sign-kNN approaches full-model test accuracy in sufficiently wide and deep networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Binary last-layer sign codes can retain classification information sufficient to approach full-model test accuracy in the tested vision classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Sign-code purity correlates with test accuracy; repulsion training can reduce purity and test accuracy while retaining high training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-coherent sign geometry is associated with generalization, and disrupting it during training can impair generalization in these models.

fits_no_version.finding: Sign corruption causes greater damage than activation-magnitude replacement with the clean sign trajectory enforced; outcomes vary by architecture and activation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested classifiers depend strongly on clean activation-sign trajectories under these channel-isolating interventions.

fits_no_version.finding: Vote bias, residual diagnostics, and activation asymmetry characterize sign-only/full-model agreement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth, width, and activation-dependent representation properties help explain when sign-only classifiers agree with full networks.

record.problems: The experiments use small-scale vision benchmarks. Some diagnostics rely on proxy quantities rather than direct estimates of conditional residual moments; the paper states the residual-scaling diagnostics are consistent with, but do not directly estimate, the condition. Several figure summaries report aggregates rather than per-condition numeric values. The paper notes its theoretical analysis centers on feedforward networks and that sign-preserving activations are the scope.
record.rows_left_out: No required version-specific rows were omitted. The text includes additional plotted diagnostics and configuration-specific tables; rows were limited to reported aggregate results and key stated exceptions to keep the record focused. Appendix E.4’s flattened sensitivity table was not expanded into separate k-by-checkpoint rows because the supplied layout does not reliably preserve all cell associations.

untested.parts: Paired random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe, including chance held-out accuracy for random labels.
Test-error trends after widening beyond the width needed for zero training error.
A reported comparison establishing convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout versus no-dropout comparisons, including training-set size and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance versus train–test gaps and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures concern different effects; this does not deny the reported sign-code findings. No version-specific verdict is warranted. The discussion about possible sign-space generalization bounds does not directly test or refute V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels under the same standard recipe.
Test error as width crosses the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization, including local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across training-set sizes or with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness compared with train–test gaps and norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples and comparing test accuracy with random removal.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.operation_detail: Compared last-hidden-layer sign-kNN test error with full-model test error.
rows.measure: Absolute sign gap Δsgn between sign-kNN and model test error.
rows.value: Δsgn becomes negligible (< 0.03) once depth and width are sufficiently large.
rows.note: The paper describes a monotonic shrinkage with increasing depth and width; this is not the training–test gap.
rows.check: The sign gap is not a versioned effect. Figure 2a covers three architecture sweeps; depth 6 and width 1024 describe the fixed FFNN configuration in Figure 2b, not this sweep.

rows.subject: FFNN, ResNet-18, and ViT (540 models aggregate)
rows.size_stated: FFNN depth 6, width 1024; standard ResNet-18; ViT depth 6, embedding dimension 256, 8 heads
rows.operation_detail: Compared last-layer sign-kNN test accuracy with full-model test accuracy.
rows.measure: Sign-kNN accuracy relative to full-model test accuracy.
rows.value: In the overparameterized regime, points cluster tightly around the diagonal with no systematic dependence on architecture, activation, or dataset.
rows.note: The paper reports the 540-model aggregate; this compares test performance, not training and test error.
rows.check: Agreement between sign-kNN and each model does not establish a convolutional-versus-fully-connected accuracy comparison. The stated factorial design implies 1620 models, inconsistent with the paper's reported 540; preserve this as a source inconsistency.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured training-set leave-one-out sign-code neighborhood purity against test accuracy across models.
rows.measure: Association between train LOO purity and test accuracy.
rows.value: Spearman ρ = 0.834; high neighborhood purity tracks generalization.
rows.note: This measured property is sign-code purity, not magnitude-aware sharpness.
rows.check: Neighborhood purity versus test accuracy does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness versus the generalization gap.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.stage_stated: trained with repulsion regularizer; maximum 2500 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Trained with within-class sign/gate repulsion regularizer Lrep.
rows.measure: Training accuracy; test accuracy; train LOO purity.
rows.baseline: Normally trained baseline test accuracy not stated numerically in this result.
rows.value: Training accuracy reaches 97%; test accuracy drops to ∼40%; train LOO purity drops to 0.34.
rows.note: A training intervention deliberately repels same-class codes; this is not a standard-training result.
rows.check: Deliberately disrupting class geometry does not test random-label fitting or another specified version.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.stage_stated: trained with repulsion regularizer; maximum 2500 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Applied repulsion regularizer and measured training and test accuracy across activations.
rows.measure: Training and test accuracy after repulsion training.
rows.baseline: Normally trained baseline accuracy not stated numerically in this result.
rows.value: Test accuracy and LOO purity sharply degrade while training accuracy remains ≥97%.
rows.note: Results summarized across these three activations.
rows.check: Repulsion training measures a different intervention from those specified in V1–V8.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.stage_stated: trained with repulsion regularizer; maximum 2500 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Applied repulsion regularizer and measured training and test accuracy.
rows.measure: Effect of repulsion on test accuracy and purity while retaining training accuracy.
rows.value: Tanh is partially robust (δ ≈ 0).
rows.note: The text does not give the corresponding numerical accuracies here.
rows.check: The reported near-zero δ describes magnitude asymmetry, not the size of the accuracy change. Tanh robustness is qualitative here.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured fraction of training points whose sign code is shared only with same-class examples.

conditions.value: grid; exact values not stated for this summary

rows.measure: Sign purity across width–depth configurations.
rows.value: Sign purity is high across much of the grid, including configurations where NC1 remains large and NC4 is poor.
rows.note: The text does not provide exact purity values in this passage.
rows.check: Sign purity and neural-collapse diagnostics measure none of the specified effects.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured sign-kNN gap and full-model versus sign-only classifier disagreement across a width–depth sweep.
rows.measure: Sign-kNN gap Δsgn and sign-only disagreement ε1 in the empirical gate-domination region.
rows.value: Above the marked region, Δsgn < 0.03 and ε1 < 0.1.
rows.note: These are sign-code/full-model comparisons, not train–test gaps.
rows.check: The width sweep reports sign-code agreement, without establishing test-error behavior beyond a zero-training-error threshold.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured full-classifier and sign-only classifier agreement at depth 1.
rows.measure: Gate-domination score and sign-only/full-model disagreement.
rows.value: Vote bias is approximately zero; Z1 < 0.23 even at width 4096.
rows.note: Depth 1 does not attain the sign-only agreement regime.
rows.check: Low gate-domination scores at depth 1 do not establish whether widening lowers test error.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured sign-only vote bias and agreement with the full classifier.
rows.measure: Fraction of inputs with positive vote bias for every competitor; agreement between sign-only and full classifiers.
rows.value: Fraction exceeds 0.80 in the overparameterized regime; it exceeds 0.85 for depth ≥4 and width ≥64, and exceeds 0.95 for depth ≥6; classifiers agree on precisely these inputs.
rows.note: The reported values concern sign-only/full-model agreement, not training–test error.
rows.check: These are classifier-agreement diagnostics. The paper's aggregate thresholds conflict with Figure 7: depth 4, width 64 gives 0.6994, and depth 6, width 64 gives 0.7844. Do not present the stated thresholds as holding uniformly across the grid.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.operation_detail: Compared a diagonal residual-scale proxy against the conditional residual moment used in the theoretical condition.
rows.measure: Median and mean of per-input residual diagnostic ratio.
rows.baseline: χ²(1) benchmark median ≈ 0.455 and mean = 1, under approximate uncorrelatedness and CLT assumptions.
rows.value: Median 0.4–0.9; mean 1.5–3.0 in the transitional regime.
rows.note: Authors state this is consistent with, but not a direct estimate of, the conditional moment condition.
rows.check: This is a residual-scale proxy diagnostic, not a measure of a specified generalization effect.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise correlations between standardized per-neuron residual contributions.
rows.measure: Mean absolute off-diagonal correlation.
rows.value: ρ̂m ≤ 0.10 for width ≤256; at width ≥512, it can increase up to ∼0.6.
rows.note: The condition changes with width; at larger widths the correlation can rise.
rows.check: Residual correlations do not measure V1–V8. The subject size must include widths at least 512 because the value includes those configurations.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured magnitude asymmetry, gate-only margin, residual noise, and gate-domination score.
rows.measure: Median gate-only margin and median gate-domination score across representative configurations.
rows.value: At width 4096, depth 12, SiLU γ̃med = 2.89 and tanh γ̃med = 0.95; SiLU Z1 ∼10 and tanh Z1 ∼0.95.
rows.note: Table 2 reports selected configurations; paper states tanh sign codes remain causally necessary despite small Z1.
rows.check: At width 4096, depth 12, Table 2 gives tanh Z1 approximately 0.4; 0.95 is its gate-only margin. The model count is inconsistent: the record says 240 aggregate, while H.4 says 240 per activation.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.operation_detail: Compared sigmoid-gate repulsion with matched sign-based repulsion.
rows.measure: Training accuracy, test accuracy, and LOO purity for sigmoid-gate repulsion; qualitative outcome of matched sign-based repulsion.
rows.value: Sigmoid-gate repulsion: training accuracy exceeds 97%, test accuracy approximately 40%, LOO purity 0.34. Matched sign-based repulsion either destabilises training or leaves enough active-set overlap for partial generalization to survive.
rows.note: The two interventions differ in regularizer proxy; separate ReLU/GELU outcomes are not numerically reported.
rows.check: This compares repulsion proxies rather than a specified version and duplicates the sigmoid-gate outcome in R4.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.size_stated: widths 4–4096, depths 1–12; selected configurations averaged over 2 seeds
rows.operation_detail: Measured magnitude asymmetry and residual noise across activation families.
rows.measure: Magnitude asymmetry δ̄ and residual noise σ̂r.
rows.value: Tanh δ̄ ≈ 0 throughout; median |µj(+1) − µj(−1)| is 0.0014, with 95 of 120 cells at gap ≤0.005; SiLU δ̄ is typically 0.4–0.95; SiLU σ̂r is larger in 118 of 120 cells.
rows.note: These properties concern sign-code decomposition, not the versioned sharpness measure.
rows.check: Activation magnitude asymmetry and residual noise are distinct from magnitude-aware weight sharpness.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Flipped selected hidden-layer signs while preserving their magnitudes.
rows.measure: Classification accuracy under sign corruption.
rows.value: Accuracy collapses to near chance (∼10%) across all eight architecture–activation conditions.
rows.uncertainty: mean ±1 s.d. over 5 draws; numerical SD not stated
rows.note: The aggregate statement covers four activations and two architectures; no per-condition accuracy is given here.
rows.check: This flips activation signs rather than removing examples or measuring weight sharpness. The stated eight-condition aggregate exceeds this row's single ResNet/ReLU condition; expand the activation condition or identify the value as an aggregate.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.operation_detail: Flipped selected hidden-layer signs while preserving their magnitudes.
rows.measure: Classification accuracy under sign corruption.
rows.value: Accuracy collapses to near chance (∼10%) across all eight architecture–activation conditions.
rows.uncertainty: mean ±1 s.d. over 5 draws; numerical SD not stated
rows.note: The aggregate statement covers four activations and two architectures; no per-condition accuracy is given here.
rows.check: Activation-sign corruption tests none of V1–V8. Four FFNN activation conditions are represented here; eight refers to both architecture families.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Replaced selected magnitudes with random |N(0,1)| draws while enforcing the clean sign trajectory at each layer.
rows.measure: Classification accuracy after magnitude replacement.
rows.value: 93–95% accuracy across all four activations.
rows.uncertainty: mean ±1 s.d. over 5 draws; numerical SD not stated
rows.note: At α=1 every magnitude in every layer is randomized; the clean signs are enforced.
rows.check: The intervention replaces activation magnitudes, not weights. It enforces cached clean signs at every layer and does not measure magnitude-aware weight sharpness.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.operation_detail: Replaced selected magnitudes with random |N(0,1)| draws while enforcing the clean sign trajectory at each layer.
rows.measure: Classification accuracy after total magnitude replacement.
rows.value: 78% accuracy.
rows.uncertainty: mean ±1 s.d. over 5 draws; numerical SD not stated
rows.note: The text gives this specific tanh result as evidence that signs remain causally necessary.
rows.check: The 80% to 78% result concerns activation-magnitude replacement with cached signs enforced, not a weight edit or specified version.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.operation_detail: Replaced selected magnitudes with random |N(0,1)| draws while enforcing the clean sign trajectory at each layer.
rows.measure: Accuracy degradation in percentage points after total magnitude replacement.
rows.value: Degradation: ReLU ∼36 pp; GELU ∼34 pp; SiLU ∼32 pp.
rows.uncertainty: mean ±1 s.d. over 5 draws; numerical SD not stated
rows.note: The paper says the FFNN retains near-full accuracy for tanh and degrades substantially for the other activations, while remaining far above sign-flip failures.
rows.check: These accuracy losses follow activation-magnitude replacement with cached signs enforced, not weight edits or a specified version.

rows.subject: FFNN
rows.operation_detail: Compared sign-kNN predictions from different neighbor counts with model accuracy.
rows.measure: Accuracy for model and sign-kNN at k=1, 3, 5, 10, 20.
rows.value: The paper states changing k from 1 to 20 alters accuracy by at most a few points; individual k results are tabulated in Appendix E.4.
rows.note: The flattened table contains model accuracies 0.817, 0.826, 0.830 and separate k columns; row-wise values are not expanded here because the table layout is compressed in the supplied text.
rows.check: Neighbor-count sensitivity tests none of V1–V8. Appendix E.4 is readable: for k=1,3,5,10,20, accuracies are respectively 0.799/0.807/0.808/0.809/0.809; 0.777/0.770/0.780/0.780/0.778; and 0.823/0.826/0.825/0.826/0.825 for the three listed checkpoints.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
